correctness.rationale: The exact invariant yields squared speed Y_A(s)=int_0^s[1+alpha(A²-s+u)]e^{beta u}du, s=A²-x²; it is positive for 0<s<=A², proving smooth simple ovals and minimal physical period. The original-time quadrant density is proportional 1/(sqrt(1-s/A²)v_A(s)), v_A=sqrt(Y_A)/A; hence T_A=2D_A/A² and M_q=I_q/D_A with I_q=int v_A^(q-1)/sqrt(1-s/A²) ds. Endpoint bounds show D_A->pi/sqrt(alpha beta). For fixed q<1 dominated convergence gives gamma^q/sec reciprocal cos(πq/2); q=1 has I_1=2A² exactly; q>1 setting u=A²-s and dominated Laplace integral yields gamma^q A sqrt(2beta/[pi(q-1)])exp[beta(q-1)A²/2]. For q=1+lambda/A², s=A²t and A^-2 log v_A(A²t)->beta t/2, with common integrable t^-1/4(1-t)^-1/2 domination for lambda in compacts, yields 2sqrt(alpha beta)/pi times F_beta(lambda)=int_0^1exp(beta lambda(1-u²)/2)du. Algebraic prefactors and period normalization checked against exact formulas; verify.py finite quadratures only corroborate. No claim at alpha=0 or q varying faster than A^-2.
